content.body:
Designed and produced well before the outbreak of WWII, the Ju 52 was ultimately used in every theatre as general transport aircraft of troops and materials by the Luftwaffe. Starting out as a single-engine civilian airliner in 1930, the Ju 52 got a much needed power boost when two more engines were added. No high performance aircraft by any stretch of the imagination, the Ju52s strengths lay in its ability to carry heavy loads as well as take off and land virtually anywhere. Ju-52's fitted with floats were used in Canada to carry huge lumber loads out of remote areas by landing on nearby lakes.
The "Tante Ju" (Auntie Ju) was a very well known and famous aircraft in all parts of the world, and served many nations as an airliner and transport. However, it was to find its greatest abilities as a military transport and cargo aircraft. It was used by both Allied forces and its originators behind the Axis curtain. Extremely docile handling at slow speeds allow the Ju-52 to operate just about anywhere, but those same advantages become its undoing in a combat zone. It makes a huge and slow moving target; a literal bullet magnet for enemy fire.
When running paratroopers to a drop zone, pick routes that are outside of normal air traffic patterns so as to remain unspotted as long as you can. Sometimes flying 'Nap Of the Earth' (as low as possible) can delay you from being detected and the Ju 52 is very good at that flight profile. Do not forget to open the door and turn on the jump light (the O key) when you are at the drop zone to let the para's know it is time to hit the silk.
The Ju 52 is a 'stand in' for a general French airborne transport craft.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Pilot 2 Co-Pilot* 3 Top Gunner
* (Currently, the co-pilot cannot fly the aircraft.)
